absent: Core mount, move, pivot, propagation change, writer hold, group identifier, namespace allocation, and path lookup internals are not shown.
Filesystem context, mount, mount namespace, mount attribute, and statmount structure layouts beyond referenced fields are not shown.
Numeric values of mount flags, attribute bits, propagation bits, atime modes, and error codes beyond names are not shown.
Lock ordering, sleep context, and full concurrency rules for namespace and mount hash locks are not shown.
Security, capability, user namespace, andreachability decision internals are not shown.
Sequence buffer management and dentry path rendering internals beyond the wrapper contract are not shown.

findings.text: Mount entry copies type device and options from user space into kernel memory, invokes the core mount operation with directory name flags and copied options, releases temporary buffers in reverse order, and returns the operation status, propagating copy failures without proceeding.

Filesystem mount creation entry validates user flags against cloexec and namespace bits, enforces admin capability for namespace creation and general mount permission otherwise, rejects attribute bits outside the allowed set, translates attributes to internal mount flags, enforces exactly one atime mode, checks that the supplied descriptor refers to a filesystem context, requires an established root and awaiting mount phase, refuses overly revealing or user restricted instances, creates the mount, and either installs it as a new namespace or as a path descriptor marked for unmount on close.

Move mount entry requires mount permission, rejects unknown flag bits and the combination of beneath with set group, maps set group and beneath to internal tree options, resolves target and source either by borrowing an open descriptor path or by filename lookup with optional empty path follow and automount handling, then delegates to a helper that applies a security check and either changes propagation grouping or performs the move.
Pivot root entry resolves both supplied paths in the current directory context requiring follow and directory semantics, then delegates to the path based pivot operation and returns its result.

Set attribute entry filters allowed lookup control bits, derives lookup behavior for automount and follow, records recursion request, parses user attributes with size and permission checks, treats an empty attribute set as a no operation, otherwise looks up the target and applies the prepared attribute change before releasing temporary identity references.

Open tree with attributes entry rejects a nonzero size without a user pointer, opens the tree, and when attributes are present prepares an attribute change where clone enables identity replacement and recursion is propagated, applies the change to the opened path only if the request is not a no operation, and publishes the descriptor on success.

Translation between user attribute bits and internal mount flags preserves readonly nosuid nodev noexec nodiratime and nosymfollow individually, while atime modes are handled separately with strict treated as the absence of internal atime bits and noatime and relatime mapped to their counterparts, rejecting any other atime combination.

Reporting translates internal mount flags back to user attributes for readonly nosuid nodev noexec nodiratime nosymfollow and atime, preferring noatime over relatime with strict as the fallback when neither is set, and adds the identity mapping indicator when the mount uses a non null mapping.

Attribute change construction allows at most one propagation mode, rejects attribute bits outside the permitted set, converts set and clear bits to internal flags, requires the full atime clear group when changing atime and forbids atime set bits without that clear group, clears prior atime state before installing the requested relatime noatime or strict mode, then delegates identity mapping construction.

Identity mapping construction is skipped when neither set nor clear requests identity handling, removal without replacement is rejected, removal alone installs the null mapping, otherwise the supplied descriptor must reference a user namespace distinct from the initial namespace with admin capability in the target, which is then retained for later allocation.

Identity mapping permission is granted immediately when no mapping is requested, otherwise it rejects reuse of the filesystem wide namespace, forbids changing an already mapped mount without explicit replacement, requires filesystem support and absence of an opt out flag, requires admin capability in the filesystem user namespace, and requires the mount to reside in an anonymous namespace.

Effective flags are computed by clearing requested bits then setting requested bits over current mount flags, and writers may remain only when the change does not newly introduce readonly and does not involve an identity mapping.

Attribute changes use a two phase walk over the target mount and optionally its descendants where preparation validates locked flag transitions and identity rules and holds writers when needed with full unwind on failure, and commitment installs identity mappings updates flags releases writer holds adjusts propagation and marks the namespace as touched, stopping after the first mount when recursion is not requested.

Application of prepared attributes requires the path to be mounted, allocates an identity mapping object when a target namespace was retained, takes the namespace lock only for propagation changes with validation of the mounted tree and preallocation of shared group identifiers, then holds the mount hash lock to revalidate and run preparation followed by commitment, cleaning allocated group identifiers on failure.

User attribute intake enforces compile time size identity for the versioned structure, rejects oversized and undersized inputs, requires mount permission, copies the variable sized structure from user space, and signals no operation when set clear and propagation are all zero.

Query scratch state holds a user buffer pointer and size, the target mount and its identity mapping, a selection mask, a root path for relative rendering, an embedded sequence file for string building, and ends with an embedded mount statistics record that itself ends in a flexible array so it must remain last.

Superblock reporting sets its mask and exposes device major and minor magic and a filtered subset of filesystem flags, while mount reporting sets its mask and exposes unique and legacy identifiers parent identifiers attribute and propagation encodings and peer and master group numbers with zero master for non slave mounts.

Propagation encoding reports shared slave and unbindable states individually and substitutes private when none apply, with a public wrapper that resolves a generic mount reference to its container before encoding.

Dominating identifier search walks the slave master chain and for each master scans its peer group returning the first peer that lives in the relevant namespace and is reachable from the supplied root, yielding zero when no such peer exists, while identifier lookup in a namespace validates both presence and unique identifier equality.

Mount root reporting renders the mount root path into the sequence buffer and fails with retry on overflow before unescaping octal escapes in place, mount point reporting renders the mount path relative to the query root treating skip as success, and the shared path helper acquires a buffer renders a path relative to a root mangles escapes commits the result and maps overlong to success while propagating other errors.

Attribute application serializes propagation changes with the namespace lock and tree validation with the mount hash lock, commitment updates flags with ordered writes and identity pointers with release semantics paired with acquire on readers, flag reporting uses ordered reads, and unmounted parent identifier reads are protected by a dedicated mount reader guard while mounted reads rely on existing stability.

Filesystem context must be in the awaiting mount phase to create a mount, rejects busy otherwise, warns when mandatory locking is present, and after successful creation is cleaned into a state equivalent to having picked an existing context without further allocation that could fail.
Namespace file test identifies namespace files by comparing the file operations pointer against the namespace file operations table.
Propagation query and dominating identifier computation and path rendering relative to a root are exposed as reusable helpers for mount status and sequence file consumers.

Creation fails closed on revealing mounts user restricted superblocks missing roots and incorrect phases, identity changes fail when the mount has already been visible, writer holds are unwound on preparation failure and always released on commitment, and string rendering signals retry on overflow rather than truncating silently.
Allowed creation attributes comprise readonly, nosuid, nodev, noexec, the atime group, nodiratime and nosymfollow.
Allowed setattr attributes comprise the creation set plus identity mapping.
Allowed setattr propagation modes comprise unbindable, private, slave and shared with at most one selected.
A mount is considered identity mapped exactly when its effective mapping differs from the global null mapping.
